question: Should OpenClaw accept a restart-specific durable SQLite audit table for restart attribution after the branch preserves current-main update restart semantics?
rationale: The remaining choice is not only code mechanics: the PR defines a new local persisted metadata boundary and fixed retention policy around restart events.

options.title: Accept After Rebase
options.body: Require the current-main restart reason promotion repair, then accept the bounded restart audit table and redaction contract as the intended operator-forensics surface.

options.title: Narrow Persisted Metadata
options.body: Ask for a smaller persisted column/payload set or stricter redaction policy before accepting the security boundary.

options.title: Defer To Broader Audit Ledger
options.body: Pause or close this restart-specific producer if maintainers want the broader audit-ledger direction to own all durable audit records first.

recommendation.title: Accept After Rebase
recommendation.body: Require the current-main restart reason promotion repair, then accept the bounded restart audit table and redaction contract as the intended operator-forensics surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway restart behavior, operator forensics, and shared state policy where recent history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
